# Native Select

The browser's own select, dressed as Koala's Select trigger. The list that opens is the operating system's: the wheel on iOS, the sheet on Android. Closed, it is indistinguishable from a Select of the same size.

```tsx
<Field>
  <FieldLabel>Timezone</FieldLabel>
  <NativeSelect defaultValue="Europe/Madrid">
    <NativeSelectOptGroup label="Americas">
      <NativeSelectOption value="America/New_York">New York (GMT−4)</NativeSelectOption>
      <NativeSelectOption value="America/Los_Angeles">Los Angeles (GMT−7)</NativeSelectOption>
      <NativeSelectOption value="America/Sao_Paulo">São Paulo (GMT−3)</NativeSelectOption>
    </NativeSelectOptGroup>
    <NativeSelectOptGroup label="Europe">
      <NativeSelectOption value="Europe/London">London (GMT+1)</NativeSelectOption>
      <NativeSelectOption value="Europe/Madrid">Madrid (GMT+2)</NativeSelectOption>
      <NativeSelectOption value="Europe/Berlin">Berlin (GMT+2)</NativeSelectOption>
    </NativeSelectOptGroup>
    <NativeSelectOptGroup label="Asia Pacific">
      <NativeSelectOption value="Asia/Tokyo">Tokyo (GMT+9)</NativeSelectOption>
      <NativeSelectOption value="Australia/Sydney">Sydney (GMT+10)</NativeSelectOption>
    </NativeSelectOptGroup>
  </NativeSelect>
  <FieldHint>Used for your reports and reminders.</FieldHint>
</Field>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli@latest init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli@latest add native-select
```

Manual: run `npm install radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/native-select/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

```tsx title="usage.tsx"
import { NativeSelect, NativeSelectOption } from "@/components/ui/native-select"

export function Example() {
  return (
    <NativeSelect name="role" defaultValue="editor">
      <NativeSelectOption value="admin">Admin</NativeSelectOption>
      <NativeSelectOption value="editor">Editor</NativeSelectOption>
      <NativeSelectOption value="viewer">Viewer</NativeSelectOption>
    </NativeSelect>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
import { NativeSelect, NativeSelectOptGroup, NativeSelectOption } from "@/components/ui/native-select"

<NativeSelect>
  <NativeSelectOption value="" disabled />
  <NativeSelectOptGroup label="…">
    <NativeSelectOption value="…" />
  </NativeSelectOptGroup>
</NativeSelect>
```

## Beside a Select

The closed control is the Select trigger, token for token: the same frame and `--surface` ground, the same caret, and the same brand border and halo once it has focus. Heights come from `size`, the scale every control shares (`sm` 32 · `md` 36 · `lg` 40px), so the two sit in a row without anyone noticing which one is native. Native on the left, Select on the right.

```tsx
<NativeSelect size="sm" defaultValue="editor">…</NativeSelect>
<Select defaultValue="editor"><SelectTrigger size="sm">…</SelectTrigger>…</Select>

<NativeSelect size="md" defaultValue="editor">…</NativeSelect>
<Select defaultValue="editor"><SelectTrigger size="md">…</SelectTrigger>…</Select>

<NativeSelect size="lg" defaultValue="editor">…</NativeSelect>
<Select defaultValue="editor"><SelectTrigger size="lg">…</SelectTrigger>…</Select>
```

## Placeholder

Make the first option the empty one (`value=""`), and `disabled` so it can't be chosen back. While it is the selected option the control reads in the muted placeholder ink at normal weight, like an empty Select; the rows in the open list keep the foreground.

```tsx
<NativeSelect defaultValue="">
  <NativeSelectOption value="" disabled>Choose a role</NativeSelectOption>
  <NativeSelectOption value="admin">Admin</NativeSelectOption>
  <NativeSelectOption value="editor">Editor</NativeSelectOption>
  <NativeSelectOption value="viewer">Viewer</NativeSelectOption>
</NativeSelect>
```

## In a form

Where a native picker is the better one: a card expiry is two short fixed lists, and on a phone the OS wheel beats any custom menu. `Form` imposes its `lg` size on every control inside it, the native selects included, so the row lines up with the security code beside it. The values post with the form, with no JavaScript required.

```tsx
<Form className="w-full max-w-sm">
  <div className="grid grid-cols-3 gap-3">
    <Field>
      <FieldLabel>Month</FieldLabel>
      <NativeSelect name="exp-month" defaultValue="">
        <NativeSelectOption value="" disabled>MM</NativeSelectOption>
        {months.map((m) => <NativeSelectOption key={m} value={m}>{m}</NativeSelectOption>)}
      </NativeSelect>
    </Field>
    <Field>
      <FieldLabel>Year</FieldLabel>
      <NativeSelect name="exp-year" defaultValue="">
        <NativeSelectOption value="" disabled>YYYY</NativeSelectOption>
        {years.map((y) => <NativeSelectOption key={y} value={y}>{y}</NativeSelectOption>)}
      </NativeSelect>
    </Field>
    <Field>
      <FieldLabel>CVC</FieldLabel>
      <InputRoot><InputField name="cvc" placeholder="123" inputMode="numeric" /></InputRoot>
    </Field>
  </div>
</Form>
```

## Error and disabled

Inside a `Field`, `hasError` turns the frame red and points `aria-describedby` at the hint, which becomes the message; `disabled` on the Field reaches the select too. Both need no wiring on the control itself.

```tsx
<Field hasError>
  <FieldLabel>Plan</FieldLabel>
  <NativeSelect defaultValue="">
    <NativeSelectOption value="" disabled>Choose a plan</NativeSelectOption>
    …
  </NativeSelect>
  <FieldHint>Pick a plan to continue.</FieldHint>
</Field>
<Field disabled>
  <FieldLabel>Billing cycle</FieldLabel>
  <NativeSelect defaultValue="annual">…</NativeSelect>
  <FieldHint>Fixed while a payment is pending.</FieldHint>
</Field>
```

## API reference

### NativeSelect

A `<select>` in a positioned frame with the caret. Every `<select>` prop but `multiple` (`name`, `value`, `onChange`, `ref`) goes on the select; `className` goes on the frame, so a width moves the caret with it.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| size | "sm" \| "md" \| "lg" | - | Height 32, 36 or 40px. Unset, it comes from a container (`Form` imposes `lg`) or density (`compact`, the default, is `sm`). |
| density | "comfortable" \| "compact" | - | Only picks the default `size` (`compact` is `sm`, `comfortable` is `md`). |

### NativeSelectOption

A native `<option>`; the OS draws it, so it takes text only. An empty-valued, `disabled` first option is the placeholder, read in muted ink while selected.

### NativeSelectOptGroup

A native `<optgroup>`; the OS draws its `label` as a heading in the list.

## FAQ

### Native Select or Select?

Native Select where the OS picker is the better one: forms used on phones, long fixed lists (years, timezones), and forms that must post without JavaScript. Select where the options need icons, flags, descriptions, a search, or the same look on every platform.

### Can I style the list that opens?

Barely, and that is the point: the operating system draws it. The rows keep the foreground ink on Windows, and the dark themes ask for the dark native picker, but icons, descriptions and custom rows need Select.

### Why no `multiple`?

A native multi-select is a box of rows you have to ctrl-click, which nobody discovers. For several values from a list, use MultiSelect.

### Why does the focus halo stay while I pick?

A native select is focused for as long as its list is open, so the halo holds through the choice the way a Select trigger's does while its menu is open.

### Where does className go?

On the frame around the select, so `w-56` or `flex-1` sizes the control and moves the caret with it. Everything else, including `ref`, goes on the `<select>`.

## Exports and dependencies

`npx koalaui-cli@latest add native-select` writes `components/ui/native-select/`. Import from `@/components/ui/native-select`:

- Components and helpers: `NativeSelect`, `NativeSelectOption`, `NativeSelectOptGroup`, `nativeSelectVariants`
- Types: `NativeSelectProps`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `density`, `field-context`, `tv`
- npm packages: `@phosphor-icons/react`
